classification.difficultyReason: Select among familiar circle-angle relationships, taking care with reflex/minor central angles and cyclic supplementary angles; no novel construction is required.

content.prompt: Find the values of the pronumerals.

spec.description: Circle, two radii and two chords; central unknown and supplied 55-degree circumference angle. Redundant vertex letters are omitted.
spec.mathematics: The marked central angle and the 55-degree circumference angle subtend the same arc.
spec.answerVisibility: Only alpha and the supplied 55-degree angle are visible.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\alpha&=2\times55^\circ\\\alpha&=110^\circ\end{aligned}$$
The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference on the same arc.

spec.description: Two chords meet on the upper-left circumference; two radii bound the smaller 34-degree central angle. A leader identifies the supplied central angle. Redundant letters are omitted.
spec.mathematics: Alpha is the circumference angle on the same minor arc as the 34-degree central angle.
spec.answerVisibility: No calculated value of alpha is shown.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\alpha&=\frac{34^\circ}{2}\\\alpha&=17^\circ\end{aligned}$$
The angle at the circumference is half the angle at the centre on the same arc.

spec.description: Four chords form two circumference angles on the same arc; the unlabelled centre point is retained in black. Redundant vertex letters are omitted.
spec.mathematics: Both marked angles subtend the same 80-degree minor arc.
spec.answerVisibility: Alpha and the supplied 40-degree angle only.

answer.worked: $\alpha=40^\circ$, because angles at the circumference subtended by the same arc are equal.

spec.description: Two radii to the ends of a lower arc and two chords from the bottom point. Alpha labels the reflex central sector. Redundant letters are omitted.
spec.mathematics: The bottom circumference angle is 130 degrees and subtends the major arc corresponding to reflex alpha.
spec.answerVisibility: The reflex sector is marked but its numerical value is hidden.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\alpha&=2\times130^\circ\\\alpha&=260^\circ\end{aligned}$$
The reflex angle at the centre is twice the circumference angle subtended by the same major arc.

spec.description: Cyclic quadrilateral with opposite angles 70 degrees and alpha. Redundant vertex letters are omitted.
spec.mathematics: Opposite angles in the cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied 70-degree angle and alpha are shown.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\alpha&=180^\circ-70^\circ\\\alpha&=110^\circ\end{aligned}$$
Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary.

spec.description: Two radii enclose a supplied reflex central angle of 268 degrees; two chords from the left circumference enclose alpha. Redundant letters are omitted.
spec.mathematics: Alpha subtends the minor arc complementary to the supplied reflex central angle.
spec.answerVisibility: The minor central angle and calculated alpha are not supplied.

answer.worked:
The smaller central angle is $360^\circ-268^\circ=92^\circ$.
$$\begin{aligned}\alpha&=\frac{92^\circ}{2}\\\alpha&=46^\circ\end{aligned}$$
The circumference angle is half the central angle on the same minor arc.
